```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(hmetad)
library(tidybayes)
library(distributional)
library(ggdist)
library(paletteer)
library(patchwork)

## display a box over a plot for animations
hide_plot <- function(plot, fill='#fafafa') {
  plot + inset_element(plot_spacer() +
                         theme(plot.background=element_rect(fill=fill)),
                       0, 0, 1, 1, align_to='full')
}

## default ggplot theme
theme_metadelta <- function(...,
                            xlim=c(0, 3), ylim=c(1, 2),
                            xbreaks=0:3, ybreaks=c(1, 1.5, 2),
                            xlab='', ylab='',
                            ink='black', paper='#fafafa') {
  list(scale_x_continuous(xlab, breaks=xbreaks, expand=expansion()),
       scale_y_continuous(ylab, breaks=ybreaks, expand=expansion()),
       theme_bw(base_size=18, ink=ink, paper=paper, ...),
       theme(plot.background=element_blank(),
             legend.background=element_blank(),
             legend.key=element_blank()),
       coord_cartesian(xlim=xlim, ylim=ylim),
       scale_color_manual('Response', limits=c(0, 1), breaks=c(0, 1),
                          ##values=c('#993bff', '#ddbdff')))
                          values=paletteer_d("fishualize::Phractocephalus_hemioliopterus")[c(1, 3)]))
}

set_theme(theme_bw(base_size=18, ink='#361a54', paper='#fafafa'))

ALPHA <- .33
PALETTE <- paletteer_d("fishualize::Phractocephalus_hemioliopterus")[c(1, 3)]
DIST_COLOR <- paletteer_d("fishualize::Phractocephalus_hemioliopterus")[4]
DELTA_COLOR <- paletteer_d("fishualize::Phractocephalus_hemioliopterus")[2]

THEME_SDT <- function(xlab='Evidence', limits=c(-2.5, 2.5), base_size=18,
                      expand=expansion(mult=c(.1, .1)),
                      ink='black', paper='#fafafa') {
  list(
    scale_x_continuous(xlab, limits=limits, breaks=seq(-4, 4, by=2), expand=expand),
    scale_color_manual('Stimulus', values=PALETTE),
    scale_fill_manual('Stimulus', values=PALETTE),
    scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0, 0)),
    theme_classic(base_size=base_size, ink=ink, paper=paper),
    theme(axis.title.y=element_blank(),
          axis.text.y=element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y=element_blank(),
          axis.line.y=element_blank())
  )
}

roc2_plot <- function(d, ..., k=NULL, shade=FALSE, point=TRUE,
                      ink='black', paper='#fafafa') {
  terms <- names(enquos(..., .named=TRUE))
  p <- NULL

  if (is.null(k)) {
    k <- n_distinct(d$confidence) + 1
  }

  d <- d |> filter(confidence <= k)
  if (length(terms) == 0) {
    p <- ggplot(d, aes(x=p_fa2, y=p_hit2))
  } else {
    p <- ggplot(d, aes(x=p_fa2, y=p_hit2,
      color=!!rlang::data_sym(first(terms)),
      group=interaction(!!!rlang::data_syms(terms))))
  }
  
  p <- p +
    geom_abline(intercept=0, slope=1, linetype='dotted') +
    coord_fixed(xlim=c(0, 1), ylim=c(0, 1), expand=FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous('P(Confidence ≥ k | Incorrect)', limits=0:1) +
    scale_y_continuous('P(Confidence ≥ k | Correct)', limits=0:1) +
    theme_bw(18, ink=ink, paper=paper) +
    theme(panel.grid=element_blank())

  if (shade) {
    p <- p + geom_polygon(fill='grey80')
  }
  if (point) {
    p <- p + geom_point()
  }

  p + geom_path()
}

type1_plot <- function(evidence, c=TRUE) {
  p <- ggplot(evidence, aes(xdist=dist_normal(mu1, sd))) +
    stat_slab(aes(fill=stimulus), color=NA, alpha=.2, scale=.8, show.legend=FALSE) +
    THEME_SDT(xlab='Type I Evidence', expand=expansion())

  if (c) {
    p <- p + geom_vline(aes(xintercept=c))
  }
  
  p
}

type2_plot <- function(evidence, response=1,
                       c=TRUE, c2=TRUE, labels=TRUE,
                       limit=2.5, label_y=0.85, expansion=0.01) {
  p <- ggplot(evidence)
  if (c) {
    p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept=first(evidence$c))
  }
  
  if (response == 'zero' || response==0 || response=='0') {
    p <- p +
      stat_slab(aes(xdist=dist_truncated(dist_normal(mu2, sd), upper=c), fill=stimulus),
                color=NA, alpha=ALPHA, scale=.8, show.legend=FALSE) +
      THEME_SDT(xlab=paste0('Type II Evidence\n("', response, '" Response)'),
                limits=c(-limit, first(evidence$c)),
                expand=expansion(add=c(0, expansion)))
    
    if (c2) {
      p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept=first(evidence$c2_0), linetype='dashed', color=PALETTE[1])
    }
    if (labels) {
      p <- p +
        geom_text(aes(x=x, y=y, label=label),
                  data=tibble(x=(first(evidence$c) + first(evidence$c2_0))/2,
                              y=label_y, label="C = low"), fontface='bold') +
        geom_text(aes(x=x, y=y, label=label),
                  data=tibble(x=(first(evidence$c2_0) - limit)/2,
                              y=label_y, label="C = high"), fontface='bold')
    }
  } else if (response == 'one' || response==1 || response=='1') {
    p <- p +
      stat_slab(aes(xdist=dist_truncated(dist_normal(mu2, sd), lower=c), fill=stimulus),
                color=NA, alpha=ALPHA, scale=.8, show.legend=FALSE) +
      THEME_SDT(xlab=paste0('Type II Evidence\n("', response, '" Response)'),
                limits=c(first(evidence$c), limit),
                expand=expansion(add=c(expansion, 0)))
    if (c2) {
      p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept=first(evidence$c2_1), linetype='dashed', color=PALETTE[2])
    }
    if (labels) {
      p <- p +
        geom_text(aes(x=x, y=y, label=label),
                  data=tibble(x=(first(evidence$c) + first(evidence$c2_1))/2,
                              y=label_y, label="C = low"), fontface='bold') +
        geom_text(aes(x=x, y=y, label=label),
                  data=tibble(x=(first(evidence$c2_1) + limit)/2,
                              y=label_y, label="C = high"), fontface='bold')
    }
  }

  p
}
```

## Confidence matters

:::{.incremental}
- Group decision-making [[@bang2017confidence; @bang2020private]]{.tiny}
- Advice giving and taking [[@hertz2017neural; @pescetelli2021confidence]]{.tiny}
- Information seeking [[@schulz2023; @vanMarcke2025]]{.tiny}
- Self-beliefs [[@katyal2025; @seow2021local]]{.tiny}
- Mental health [[@katyal2026; @hoven2019; @rouault2018psychiatric]]{.tiny}
:::

# A problem {.dark}

[We don't know how to measure confidence bias!]{.fragment}


## An empirical approach

If we're interested in one's overall level of confidence, 
let's simply compute mean confidence!

:::{.tiny}
<br>
:::

:::{.fragment}
$$
\mathbb{E}\left[C\right] = \frac{1}{N}\sum_n C_n = \sum_c P(C=c) c
$$
:::

:::{.fragment .fade-out style="background-color: #fafafa;" .absolute bottom=275 right=160 width=350 height=125}

:::

:::{.tiny}
<br>
:::

[**Pro:** high face validity]{.fragment .smaller}

[**Con:** confounded with Type I performance]{.fragment .smaller}

## Quantifying Type I decisions

:::{.tiny}
<br>
:::

:::{.columns}
::::{.column width="40%" .fragment .dark .box .much-smaller fragment-index=2}
### Sensitivity ($d'$)

How much do responses distinguish between stimuli?
::::

::::{.column width="10%"}
::::

::::{.column width="40%" .fragment .dark .box .much-smaller fragment-index=3}
### Response Bias ($c$)

Is one response more likely overall?
::::
:::

:::{style="height: 10px; display: block;"}

:::

:::{.r-stack}
::::{.fragment fragment-index=1}
```{r}
#| label: fig_evidence_1
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3
evidence <- tibble(stimulus=factor(0:1),
                   d_prime=1.5, c=0.5, meta_d_prime=1,
                   mu1=c(-1, 1)*d_prime/2, sd=1,
                   mu2=c(-1, 1)*meta_d_prime/2,
                   c2_0=-1, c2_1=1)

p <- type1_plot(evidence, c=FALSE)
p
```

## Quantifying Type I decisions

<br>

:::{.much-smaller}
|                  |   Stimulus = 0    | Stimulus = 1 |
|:----------------:|:-----------------:|:------------:|
| **Response = 0** | Correct Rejection |     Miss     |
| **Response = 1** |    False Alarm    |     Hit      |
:::


::: { .tiny .right .bottom}
@green1966
:::


## Quantifying Type II decisions

<br>

:::{.r-stack .much-smaller}
::::{.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=1 }
|                  |   Stimulus = 0    | Stimulus = 1 |
|:----------------:|:-----------------:|:------------:|
| **Response = 0** | Correct Rejection |     Miss     |
| **Response = 1** |    False Alarm    |     Hit      |
::::

::::{.fragment fragment-index=1}
|                       |   Accuracy = 0      | Accuracy = 1  |
|:---------------------:|:-------------------:|:-------------:|
| **Confidence = low**  | Correct Rejection 2 |     Miss 2    |
| **Confidence = high** |    False Alarm 2    |     Hit 2     |
::::
:::

<br>

:::{.fragment fragment-index=2}
We can extend signal detection theory<br>to model confidence ratings!
:::

::: { .tiny .right .bottom}
@fleming2014
:::


# The meta-d' model of confidence ratings {.dark}

## The meta-d' model

:::{.r-stack}
```{r}
#| label: type2_evidence_1
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
p.type1 <- type1_plot(evidence)
p.type2.0 <- type2_plot(evidence, response=0)
p.type2.1 <- type2_plot(evidence, response=1, c2=FALSE, labels=FALSE)
offset <- (first(evidence$c)+2.5) / 5

p.type1 /
   (hide_plot(p.type2.0) | hide_plot(p.type2.1)) +
      plot_layout(widths=c(offset, 1-offset))
```

## The meta-d' model

We can directly compare sensitivity<br>for Type I and Type II decisions:

:::{.tiny}
<br>
:::

:::{.fragment}
::::{.larger}
$$
\begin{align*}
M &= \frac{\textrm{meta-}d'}{d'}
\end{align*}
$$
::::

::::{style="color: #993bff;"}
[metacognitive sensitivity]{.tiny .absolute bottom=325 left=750}
[Type I sensitivity]{.tiny .absolute bottom=250 left=750}

:::::{.tiny .absolute bottom=275 left=150 style="text-align: right;"}
metacognitive<br>efficiency
:::::
::::
:::

[$M$-ratio is an independent measure of <br>
the relationship between confidence and accuracy]{.fragment}

# Metacognitive bias {.dark}


## $m$-distance

<br>

:::{.r-stack}

```{r}
#| label: mdistance_4
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4
evidence.bias2 <- tibble(stimulus=factor(0:1),
                         d_prime=1.5, c=0.5, meta_d_prime=1,
                         mu1=c(-1, 1)*d_prime/2, sd=1,
                         mu2=c(-1, 1)*meta_d_prime/2,
                         c2_0=-.25, c2_1=.9)

p.type2.0 <- type2_plot(evidence.bias2, response=0)
p.type2.1 <- type2_plot(evidence.bias2, response=1)

((p.type2.0 +
    geom_errorbar(aes(y=y, xmin=xmin, xmax=xmax),
                  data=tibble(y=.95, xmin=first(evidence.bias2$c2_0)+.05,
                              xmax=first(evidence.bias2$c)-.05),
                  color='#ba82ff', width=.05, inherit.aes=FALSE)) |
   (p.type2.1 +
      geom_errorbar(aes(y=y, xmin=xmin, xmax=xmax),
                    data=tibble(y=.95, xmin=first(evidence.bias2$c)+.05,
                                xmax=first(evidence.bias2$c2_1)-.05),
                    color='#ba82ff', width=.05, inherit.aes=FALSE))) +
  plot_layout(widths=c(offset, 1-offset))
```
::::
:::



:::{.tiny .right .bottom}
@sherman2018
:::


## $m$-distance

<br>

:::{.columns .much-smaller}
::::{.column width="50%"}
$$
m\textrm{-distance}_0 = \frac{\textrm{meta-}c - \textrm{meta-}c_2^0}{\textrm{meta-}d'}
$$
::::

::::{.column width="50%"}
$$
m\textrm{-distance}_1 = \frac{\textrm{meta-}c_2^1 - \textrm{meta-}c}{\textrm{meta-}d'}
$$
::::
:::

<br>

[**Pro:** independent of Type I criterion]{.fragment .smaller}

[**Con:** only defined for models with two confidence levels]{.fragment .smaller}

[**Con:** still confounded with Type I performance]{.fragment .smaller}

:::{.tiny .right .bottom}
@sherman2018
:::


## meta-$\Delta$

:::{.tiny}
<br>
:::

**Same idea, with two adjustments:**

:::{.incremental .much-smaller}
  1. Don't normalize distances by meta-$d'$ [@dijkstra2024]
  2. Take the average of all confidence criteria
:::

:::{.r-stack}
::::{.fragment .fade-in-then-out}
\begin{align*}
    \textrm{meta-}\Delta_r &= \left|\frac{1}{K-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K-1}\left[\textrm{meta-}c_{2,k}^r\right] - \textrm{meta-}c\right|
\end{align*}
:::

::::{.fragment}
\begin{align*}
    \textrm{meta-}\Delta_r &= \sum_{k=1}^{K-1} \frac{K - k}{K-1}\textrm{dmeta-}c_{2,k}^r
\end{align*}
::::
:::


# Does this idea work? {.dark}

## Both measures are sensitive to metacognitive bias {.smaller}

:::{.r-stack}
::::{.fragment}
```{r}

  ggplot(aes(x=c2_0_diff, y=value, color=response)) +
```

## meta-$\Delta$ is reliable for one month

```{r}
#| label: reliability_models
#| include: false
pairs_plot <- function(draws, draws.cor, session1, session2, variable, label=NULL,
                       text_x=NULL, text_y=NULL, text_size=4,
                       size=1, linewidth=.1, alpha=.1, lims=c(0, 3)) {
  if (is.null(text_x))
    text_x <- lims[1] + (lims[2]-lims[1])*3/4
  if (is.null(text_y))
    text_y <- lims[1] + (lims[2]-lims[1])/8

  sessions_to_days <- tibble(
    session=seq_len(4),
    day=c('1', '3/5', '7', '31')
  )
  day1 <- recode_values(session1, from=sessions_to_days$session, to=sessions_to_days$day)
  day2 <- recode_values(session2, from=sessions_to_days$session, to=sessions_to_days$day)
  
  draws |>
    filter(session %in% c(session1, session2)) |>
    median_qi(.value) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from=session, values_from=c(.value, .lower, .upper)) |>
    ggplot() +
    aes_string(x=paste0('.value_', session1), y=paste0('.value_', session2)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes_string(xmin=paste0('.lower_', session1),
                             xmax=paste0('.upper_', session1)),
                  linewidth=linewidth, alpha=alpha) +
    geom_errorbar(aes_string(ymin=paste0('.lower_', session2),
                             ymax=paste0('.upper_', session2)),
                  linewidth=linewidth, alpha=alpha) +
    geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype='dashed') +
    geom_point(size=size) +
    xlab(parse(text=paste0(label, '~(Day~', day1, ')'))) +
    ylab(parse(text=paste0(label, '~(Day~', day2, ')'))) +
    geom_label(aes_string(x='x', y='y', label=paste0('r_', session1, '_', session2)),
               data=draws.cor |>
                 mutate(x=text_x, y=text_y),
               hjust=.5, vjust=.5, size=text_size) +
    coord_fixed(xlim=lims, ylim=lims, expand=FALSE) +
    theme_bw(base_size=18, ink='#361a54', paper='#fafafa') +
    theme(panel.border=element_rect(linewidth=1.5),
          axis.line=element_blank())
}

m.reliability <- readRDS('../reliability.rds')

## obtain model estimates
draws.linpred <- m.reliability$data |>
  expand(participant, session) |>
  add_metacognitive_bias_draws(m.reliability, by_response=FALSE) |>
  group_by(participant, session) |>
  select(-.row) |>
  rename(.value=metacognitive_bias)

## compute posteriors over test-retest correlations
draws.cor <- draws.linpred |>
  pivot_wider(names_from=session, values_from=.value, names_prefix='session') |>
  group_by(.draw) |>
  summarize(r12=cor(session1, session2, use='complete.obs'),
            r13=cor(session1, session3, use='complete.obs'),
            r14=cor(session1, session4, use='complete.obs')) |>
  median_qi(r12, r13, r14) |>
  mutate(r_1_2=sprintf('r = %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]', r12, r12.lower, r12.upper),
         r_1_3=sprintf('r = %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]', r13, r13.lower, r13.upper),
         r_1_4=sprintf('r = %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]', r14, r14.lower, r14.upper)) |>
  select(r_1_2, r_1_3, r_1_4)
```

## Conclusions

<br>
<br>

:::{.incremental .much-smaller}
1. Mean confidence is **not** a valid measure of metacognitive bias
2. Metacognitive bias seems important, but previous studies are subject to performance confounds
3. For those already using $M$-ratio to quantify metacognitive efficiency, meta-$\Delta$ provides an **independent**, **unbiased**, and **highly reliable**<br>measure of metacognitive bias
:::


## `hmetad`: an `R` package for hierarchical Bayesian modeling of confidence ratings {.dark}

:::{.columns}

::::{.column width="60%"}

:::::{.tiny}
<br>
:::::

![](figures/hmetad_qr.svg){.center-horizontally width="50%"}
::::


::::{.column width="35%" .much-smaller}
:::::{style="font-size: 0.15em"}
<br>
:::::

``` r
## fit a multilevel meta-d' model
m <- fit_metad(
  bf(
    N ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
    dprime ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
    c ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
    metac2zero1diff ~ 1 + (1 | participant),
    metac2one1diff ~ 1 + (1 | participant)
  ), data=d, ...
)

## compute meta-delta by participant
d |>
  distinct(participant) |>
  add_metacognitive_bias_draws(m) |>
  median_qi()
```
